standard_prerequisites.name: The annihilation of the Tor modules above the number of generators of the ideal by a fixed power of the ideal, uniformly in the module and the exponent
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Author lemma lemma-annihilates-tors, whose statement is reproduced verbatim as a context span of this card (source lines 4668-4675)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the single constant c_1 used in the definition of the invariant of the module and in the diagram of the induction step.

standard_prerequisites.name: The vanishing of the Tor maps for a module annihilated by a fixed power of the ideal, again uniformly in the module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Author lemma lemma-maps-zero-fixed-torsion, whose statement is reproduced verbatim as a context span of this card (source lines 4510-4519)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the constants that give the base case of the induction.

core_obligations: Define the invariant: with the constant c_1 of the annihilation lemma and a choice I = (a_1, \ldots, a_t), the proof measures a module by the number of generators whose c_1-th power already acts as zero on it, and states the assertion of the lemma for each lower bound s on that number (proof lines 4730-4742)

Base case: a module on which all t of those powers vanish is annihilated by an explicit power of I, and the vanishing lemma for modules annihilated by a fixed power of the ideal gives the assertion for all the required degrees at once (proof lines 4745-4751)

Induction step: for a module whose invariant is exactly s the proof picks a generator acting nontrivially, uses the exact sequence of the kernel and the quotient of multiplication by its c_1-th power, and applies the induction hypothesis to both ends, which have strictly larger invariant (proof lines 4754-4763)

The sandwiching: the resulting diagram of Tor modules with exact rows and columns has one arrow zero by the choice of c_1, so the middle module is sandwiched between a quotient of one of the end terms and a submodule of the other, and the induction hypothesis gives the assertion with the stated shift of the constants (proof lines 4764-4784)
proof_roadmap: 取 lemma-annihilates-tors 的常数 c_1；令 ℓ(M) 为满足 a_i^{c_1} 在 M 上为零的下标个数，并对 s = t, t-1, …, 0 作降序归纳，命题 H_s 断言：存在 N, c 使得对一切 ℓ(M) ≥ s 的模 M 和 i = 0..s，映射 Tor_{t+1+i}(M, A/I^n) → Tor_{t+1+i}(M, A/I^{n-c}) 在 n ≥ N 时为零。
基例 s = t 用 lemma-maps-zero-fixed-torsion 的常数；归纳步对 ℓ(M) = s 取 a_i^{c_1} 在 M 上非零，用 0 → M[a_i^{c_1}] → M → M → M/a_i^{c_1}M → 0 的 Tor 图表，舍入夹逼后取 N + c 与 2c。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is a uniformity assertion with no further hypothesis on the module: above the degree given by an upper bound t for the number of generators of the ideal, the Tor maps between two powers of the ideal vanish for all modules and all sufficiently large exponents, with constants depending only on the ideal (author lemma at source lines 4713-4722, label lemma-tor-maps-vanish). The proof (source lines 4724-4785) is a descending induction on an invariant of the module that counts the generators whose fixed power already acts as zero, with the base case supplied by the vanishing lemma for modules annihilated by a power of the ideal and the induction step organised around the exact sequence of the kernel and the quotient of multiplication by that power; the two end terms have strictly larger invariant and the conclusion is read off from a diagram of Tor modules with one arrow zero by construction (proof lines 4764-4784). The invariant, the induction and the sandwiching are the content; the author closes with the standard remark that routine details are omitted. H3.
